latest_evidence.scope: One dedicated role-local scratch file. Baseline had effect_counter=0 and no committed intent. A single expected-blob update committed intent_id cross-field-r250-effect-1 and effect_counter=1. For retry logic, the update acknowledgement was not used as authority; a fresh path read reconstructed state, found the same intent_id already committed and effect_counter=1, so the protocol suppressed a second mutation. No duplicate write call was issued.
latest_evidence.semantic_conclusion: Within this exact provider-specific role-local scope, combining a durable idempotency key with fresh read-before-write reconstruction suppresses a duplicate retry after a simulated lost acknowledgement. This complements r249 stale-SHA rejection evidence. It does not prove behavior under an actual network response loss, concurrent same-intent first writers, provider-independent persistence, or full Phase-1 parity.
